title: Nem tud vs. Nem lehet: Two Different Kinds of "Can't"

sections.title: Lacking a skill vs. the situation not allowing it
sections.content: English uses "can't" for two very different ideas, and Hungarian keeps them apart. nem tud (+ infinitive, conjugated for the person) means the PERSON lacks the ability — a skill they don't have. nem lehet (+ infinitive, never conjugated) means the SITUATION makes it impossible right now — nothing to do with anyone's ability. Mixing them up is one of the most common A2 mistakes, so it's worth slowing down here.

sections.title: nem tud vs. nem lehet
rows: I can't swim. (I never learned — my ability.)
Ma nem lehet úszni, mert zárva van az uszoda.
You can't swim today, because the pool is closed. (the situation, not your ability)
I can't drive. (I don't have that skill.)
You can't drive, because it's snowing. (the road conditions)

items.spanish: Petra tud úszni, de ma nem lehet, mert zárva van az uszoda.
items.english: Petra can swim (she has the ability), but today it's not possible (the pool is closed).

items.spanish: Nem tudok elmenni a partira, mert beteg vagyok.
items.english: I can't go to the party, because I'm sick. (about me)

items.spanish: Ma nem lehet bemenni az irodába, mert elromlott a lift.
items.english: You can't get into the office today, because the elevator is broken. (about the situation)

sections.content: Ask yourself: is the missing piece about the PERSON (a skill, a license, being sick) or about the PLACE/CIRCUMSTANCE (closed, broken, bad weather)? Person → nem tud, conjugated. Situation → nem lehet, always the same word.
